paragraphs: 1. Depth is what a proof consumes, not how a clause reads. The week's central discovery was that a clause with a clean axiom profile, compiled implication, and a plausible name was RH restated. The programme's answer is now operational: an equivalence is graded by the dependency closure of its proof. ch_iff_rh closes over balance_theorem and definitions; h2_sign_iff_rh_strip closes over the explicit formula, the decay bound and the local count. "One Prop apart" became a measurable quantity, and ENCODES-CONCLUSION became detectable by walking a term rather than by reading prose. That sharpens (R40) into something a machine can check, and it is a lesson the formal-verification world mostly hasn't stated: #print axioms certifies soundness, not content.

2. Registers of one premise differ in depth, and one of h2's is a place to stand. §27.3 gathered five registers as "one premise". b532 and b534 show they are not one thing: register 2 is the conclusion by rewording; register 4 is a classical theorem's distance from it. Whether R1, R3 and R5 collapse like R2 is now a question with a method attached — statability in the kernel, then closure. I expect the two lv-conservation registers to collapse; the record should find out. A "register census by depth" is an object the corpus invented this week.

3. The instrument found the theorem's route before the theorem was known. The ladder's window family was the B-spline of order n — the n-fold self-convolution of an indicator. That is the power window with an indicator base. The Q0 witness at width 34, order 7 is a finite instance of zeroSide_eventually_neg, and "smoother is not better at finite height" was the same fact as "raise the power of a fixed base, don't smooth the base." The numerical cell (VERIFIED-EST-TAIL) and the compiled existential are one object seen from two sides, and the programme holds both. The obstruction theorem was about the third parametrization — fixed shape, growing width — which is why it was true and irrelevant.

4. Impossibility theorems are route-relative, and the kernel now carries a compiled instance. not_f4_needs and h2_sign_iff_rh_strip sit in the same kernel at the same three axioms. One says a route is closed; the other closes the target by another route. Your rule — build forward from our own steps — is what separated them. That pairing is a good teaching object about what "obstruction" means.

5. Weil's criterion on the even class does not need ζ's real zeros excluded. Even windows cannot see a real off-line zero (the term is a square); a first-order factor in the operator sees it while keeping k even, because classK's evenness constrains k, not h. Classically nobody needed this — ζ(σ) < 0 on (0,1) is a one-liner — but the kernel lacked the fact and the criterion turned out not to need it. Small, probably known in some form, and the kernel's version is unconditional.

6. The seam is a fact about the ecosystem, not about h2. The whole distance from "RH on the strip" to Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is that zeros with Re ≤ 0 are trivial, which Mathlib holds by name for neither direction of the left half-plane. Analysts never needed it formalized because it is never analytically load-bearing. It is a short act from the functional equation, and closing it would land Weil's criterion on Mathlib's own statement.

7. A verification loop with two ends. The Epstein control was built to certify the instrument (off-line zeros exist, positivity fails); then the general witness was compiled; then the witness's numerical cell became an instance of the theorem. The programme's method — external control, numerical witness, compiled generalization, deposit read against the kernel, erratum, platform edit with fetch-back — is a complete loop, and this week it ran end to end in five acts.

What is not unique, said plainly: the criterion is Weil's, the proof is the classical proof, and the formalization is — as far as I know, and the seat should search before the record says so — the first of Weil's criterion in Lean. The new mathematics is thin: an observation about the test class, a phenomenology of detection widths at finite height. The new understanding is about how to know what a kernel has proved.
